meta.description: The official API for TAIRED CBT question bank.

data.question: What is the primary purpose of Object Oriented Programming?
data.a: To execute code faster than procedural programming
data.b: To model real-world entities and their interactions within a digital environment
data.c: To eliminate the need for functions in code
data.d: To replace all data structures with objects

data.question: In Python, what keyword is used to create a class?
data.b: define

data.question: Which of the following best describes an object in Python?
data.b: A specific instance of a class with its own data
data.d: A built-in data type like list or dict

data.question: What three components does an object consist of?
data.b: State, behavior, identity

data.question: What does the init method do in a Python class?
data.b: Initializes a new object's attributes when created
data.c: Converts an object to a string

data.question: In the Dog class example, what is species = "Canine" considered?
data.b: A local variable

data.question: What is inheritance in Python?
data.a: Deleting a parent class from memory
data.b: A child class inheriting attributes and methods from a parent class
data.d: Creating multiple instances of the same class

data.question: Which type of inheritance involves a child class inheriting from two or more parent classes?
data.b: Multilevel inheritance

data.question: In the code class Labrador(Dog):, what is Labrador?
data.b: The child class

data.question: What is polymorphism in Python?
data.a: Having only one method per class
data.b: Methods with the same name behaving differently based on the object
data.d: Storing multiple data types in a single variable

data.question: Which type of polymorphism is determined during program execution (run-time)?
data.b: Method overloading

data.question: What is encapsulation?
data.b: Bundling data and methods within a class and restricting access to some components
data.c: Allowing any function to modify any variable
data.d: Converting a class into a module

data.question: In Python, how is a protected member typically denoted?
data.b: With one underscore prefix (e.g., _breed)

data.question: How is a private member denoted in Python classes?
data.b: With two underscores prefix (e.g., __age)

data.question: What is abstraction in OOP?
data.b: Hiding internal implementation details while exposing only necessary functionality
data.c: Creating as many classes as possible
data.d: Removing all methods from a class

data.question: What is an abstract class?
data.a: A class that can be instantiated directly
data.b: A class that contains only concrete methods
data.c: A class that cannot be instantiated directly and is meant to be extended by subclasses

data.question: Which module in Python is used to create abstract base classes?
data.b: abstract

data.question: What decorator is used to mark a method as abstract in Python?
data.b: @abstract

data.question: What happens if you try to instantiate an abstract class directly?
data.a: The class is created with empty methods
data.b: Python returns None
data.d: The abstract methods are automatically implemented

data.question: What is a concrete method in an abstract class?
data.a: A method that must be overridden by subclasses
data.b: A method with a full implementation that subclasses can inherit and use directly
data.c: A method that raises an error if called
data.d: A method that cannot be inherited

data.question: What is the scope of a variable defined at the top level of a module?
data.b: Enclosing scope only

data.question: What is an iterator in Python?
data.b: An object that allows sequential access to elements in a collection
data.c: A type of variable that stores multiple values

data.question: Which two methods are the primary methods of Python iterators?
data.b: begin() and end()

data.question: What does the iter function do?
data.b: It creates an iterator object from an iterable
data.d: It counts the number of items in a collection

data.question: What does the next function do?
data.a: It restarts the iterator from the beginning
data.b: It returns the next item from an iterator
data.d: It jumps to the last item

data.question: What exception is raised when next is called on an iterator with no more items?
data.b: KeyError

data.question: What is an iterable in Python?
data.a: An object that can be looped over, like a list or tuple
data.b: A function that performs iteration

data.question: What is the difference between an iterator and an iterable?
data.b: An iterable can be looped over; an iterator does the looping and keeps state
data.c: An iterator can be looped over; an iterable cannot
data.d: An iterable uses more memory than an iterator

data.question: What does the enumerate function do?
data.a: It counts the number of items in a list
data.b: It returns pairs of index and value while looping
data.c: It sorts a list in ascending order

data.question: What is the output of list(enumerate(["a", "b", "c"]))?
How can you change the starting index of enumerate?
data.b: Use the index parameter

data.question: What is a stack in data structures?
data.b: Last In First Out (LIFO)

data.question: Which method adds an item to the top of a stack implemented with a list?
data.b: add()

data.question: Which method removes an item from the top of a stack implemented with a list?
data.b: delete()

data.question: What does LIFO stand for?
data.b: First In Last Out

data.question: Which of the following describes a key difference between SOAP and REST?
data.a: SOAP is an architectural style, while REST is a strict protocol
data.b: SOAP only allows JSON, while REST supports multiple formats
data.c: SOAP only allows XML, while REST supports multiple formats
data.d: SOAP is used for local APIs, while REST is for web APIs

data.question: Which queue operation is used to get the front item without removing it?
data.b: dequeue

data.question: How many architectural constraints does REST have for building applications that work over HTTP?
data.b: Five

data.question: Why is the enumerate function commonly used in Python loops?
data.a: To load the entire collection into memory at once
data.b: To replace the need for manually using a counter variable

data.question: Which of the following methods is typically used for API authentication?
data.b: Using API keys or OAuth tokens

data.question: 153. What is rate limiting in API usage?
data.b: Limiting the number of requests a client can make in a given time period

data.question: 154. How can you handle API errors gracefully in Python?
data.b: Use try-except blocks to catch exceptions

data.question: 155. What is the purpose of the API documentation?
data.b: To explain how to use the API, including endpoints, parameters, and authentication

data.question: 156. Which status code indicates that authentication is required and has failed or not been provided?
157. What is the base URL of an API?
data.b: The common prefix for all API endpoints

data.question: 158. What does the following code do? try: response = requests.get(url, timeout=5) except requests.exceptions.Timeout: print("Request timed out")
data.b: It sends a request and catches a timeout exception if the request takes longer than 5 seconds
data.c: It always prints Request timed out

data.question: 159. What is the purpose of the params parameter in requests.get?
data.a: To send data in the request body
data.b: To add query parameters to the URL

data.question: 160. What is an SDK in relation to APIs?
data.b: A Software Development Kit that provides tools and libraries to work with an API

data.question: 161. What is searching in computer science?
data.a: Sorting data in a specific order
data.b: Locating a target element within a collection of data

data.question: 162. Which membership operator returns True if an element is present in a sequence?
data.b: in

data.question: 163. What does the not in operator do?
data.a: Returns True if an element is present
data.b: Returns True if an element is not present in the sequence

data.question: 164. What is the output of print('apple' in ['orange', 'apple', 'grape'])?
data.b: True

data.question: 165. What is the main limitation of membership operators for searching?
data.b: They only return True or False, not the position of the element
data.d: They cannot be used with strings

data.question: 166. What is linear search?
data.a: A search algorithm that repeatedly divides the search interval in half
data.b: A search algorithm that checks each element sequentially until the target is found
data.c: A search algorithm that jumps ahead by fixed steps
data.d: A search algorithm that uses a formula to guess the position

data.question: 167. What is the time complexity of linear search in the worst case?
data.b: O(log n)

data.question: What are the two critical components of recursion in Python?
data.b: Iterative Case and Function Case

data.question: What is the time complexity of Merge sort in all cases?
data.b: O(n log n)

data.question: Which sorting algorithm picks an element as a pivot and partitions the array around it?
data.b: Selection sort

data.question: How does Selection sort work?
data.a: By continuously dividing the array into two halves
data.b: By picking a pivot element and partitioning the array
data.c: By comparing adjacent elements and swapping them
data.d: By repeatedly selecting the smallest element from the unsorted portion and swapping it with the first unsorted element

data.question: In Insertion sort, which element does the algorithm typically start with, assuming the preceding elements are already sorted?
data.b: The second element

data.question: What is merge sort?
data.a: A sorting algorithm that uses adjacent comparisons
data.b: A divide and conquer algorithm that divides the array into halves, sorts them, and merges
data.c: A sorting algorithm that selects a pivot
data.d: An algorithm that only works on small arrays

data.question: What is quick sort?
data.a: A divide and conquer algorithm that picks a pivot and partitions the array around it
data.b: A sorting algorithm that uses adjacent comparisons
data.c: An algorithm that only works on strings

data.question: What are the three main steps in quick sort?
data.b: Choose a pivot, partition the array, recursively call on sub-arrays

data.question: What is the base case for recursion in quick sort?
data.a: When the array has one element or is empty
data.b: When the array has 10 elements
data.c: When the pivot is the largest element

data.question: What is a recursive function?
data.b: A function that calls another function
data.d: A function that only runs once

data.question: What are the two critical components of recursion?
data.b: Base case and recursive case

data.question: What is the base case in a recursive function?
data.a: The condition that causes infinite recursion
data.b: The condition that terminates the recursion

data.question: What happens if a recursive function has no base case?
data.b: It returns None
data.c: It calls itself forever, causing a RecursionError
data.d: It automatically adds a base case

data.question: What is the output of factorial(5) using the recursive factorial function?
What is the base case in the recursive factorial function?
data.b: num == 1

data.question: What is the recursive case in the factorial function?
data.b: num * factorial(num - 1)

data.question: What is the Fibonacci sequence?
What is the recursive formula for Fibonacci numbers?
What is one disadvantage of recursion?
data.a: It always runs faster than iteration
data.b: It uses less memory than iteration
data.c: Each recursive call adds a new layer to the stack, causing memory overhead

data.question: What is an advantage of recursion?
data.b: It can reduce code length for problems naturally recursive like tree traversals
data.c: It is always faster than iteration

data.question: What is the difference between recursion and iteration?
data.a: Recursion uses loops; iteration uses function calls
data.b: Recursion uses function calls; iteration uses loops

data.question: What is the merge function in merge sort responsible for?
data.b: Merging two sorted sub-arrays into one sorted array

data.question: What is the partition function in quick sort responsible for?
data.b: Rearranging elements around the pivot and returning the pivot's final position

data.question: What is the time complexity of bubble sort in the worst case?
data.b: O(n log n)

data.question: What is the output of the following code? try: print("try") except: print("except") else: print("else")
data.b: try except

data.question: What is the output of the following code? try: x=1/0 except ZeroDivisionError: print("caught") else: print("no error")
data.b: no error

data.question: What does the raise statement do?
data.b: It manually raises an exception

data.question: What is the syntax for raising an exception?
data.b: throw Exception

data.question: Can you create your own custom exceptions in Python?
data.a: No, only built-in exceptions are allowed
data.b: Yes, by creating a class that inherits from the built-in Exception class
data.c: Yes, but only using the except keyword
data.d: No, Python does not support user-defined exceptions

data.question: What is BaseException in Python?
data.a: A specific error for division by zero
data.b: The base class for all built-in exceptions

data.question: What is ArithmeticError?
data.a: An error that occurs when a file is not found
data.b: The base class for arithmetic errors like ZeroDivisionError and OverflowError

data.question: When is AssertionError raised?
data.a: When a file is not found
data.b: When an assert statement fails
data.d: When a variable is not defined

data.question: When is AttributeError raised?
data.a: When a file is not found
data.b: When an attribute reference or assignment fails
data.c: When a variable is not defined
data.d: When a list index is out of range

data.question: When is EOFError raised?
data.a: When a file is not found
data.b: When the input() function hits an end-of-file condition without reading any data
data.c: When a variable is not defined

data.question: When is ImportError raised?
data.a: When a variable is not defined
data.b: When an import statement fails to load a module
data.c: When a file is not found
data.d: When a function is called with wrong arguments

data.question: What is LookupError?
data.a: A specific error for missing files
data.b: A base class for errors that occur when a collection lookup fails

data.question: When is MemoryError raised?
data.a: When a file is too large
data.b: When the program runs out of memory
data.d: When a function is called recursively

data.question: When is NameError raised?
data.a: When a file is not found
data.b: When a local or global name is not found
data.c: When a list index is out of range
data.d: When a function argument is invalid

data.question: When is OSError raised?
data.a: When a system-level problem occurs, like failing to find a file or running out of disk space
data.b: When a variable is not defined
data.c: When a list index is out of range

data.question: When is RuntimeError raised?
data.a: When an error does not fit into any other specific category
data.b: When a file is not found
data.c: When a variable is not defined
data.d: When a function is called correctly

data.question: What is StopIteration used for?
data.a: To stop the entire Python program
data.b: To signal that an iterator has no more items to return

data.question: When is SyntaxError raised?
data.a: When the code has improper syntax
data.b: When a file is not found

data.d: When a list index is out of range

data.question: When is TypeError raised?
data.a: When an operation is performed on an object of the wrong type

data.c: When a variable is not defined
data.d: When a list index is out of range

data.question: When is ValueError raised?
data.a: When a function receives an argument of the correct type but with an invalid value

data.question: What does GUI stand for?
data.b: General User Integration

data.question: What is a GUI?
data.a: A text-based interface for typing commands
data.b: An interface that uses visual indications and graphical elements like buttons and checkboxes

data.question: What was used for computer interaction before GUIs?
data.b: Touch screens
data.c: Text-based commands typed into a command-line interface

data.question: Which GUI toolkit comes built-in with Python?
data.b: wxPython

data.question: What is the first step in creating a GUI using tkinter?
data.b: Import the tkinter module

data.question: What does the Tk constructor do in tkinter?
data.b: Creates the main window of the GUI

data.question: What does the mainloop method do in tkinter?
data.b: Destroys all widgets
data.c: Keeps the window open and running, waiting for user events

data.question: What is a widget in tkinter?
data.b: A graphical user interface control like a button or label

data.question: Which widget is used to display a single line of text or an image?
data.b: Entry

data.question: Which widget is used to accept a single line of text input from the user?
data.b: Entry

data.question: Which widget is used for multi-line text input?
data.b: Label

data.question: Which widget is clicked to trigger an action?
data.b: Entry

data.question: What is the syntax for creating a Label widget?
data.b: label = Label(root, text="Hello")

data.question: What is the pack method used for?
data.b: To arrange widgets in rows or columns to optimize the parent area
data.c: To change the color of a widget
data.d: To bind an event to a widget

data.question: What is the grid method used for?
data.a: To pack widgets in rows or columns

data.c: To place widgets at absolute positions

data.question: What is the place method used for?
data.b: To arrange widgets in a grid

data.question: Which geometry manager must be used exclusively and cannot be mixed with others in the same master window?
data.a: Only pack and grid can be mixed

data.question: What does the Checkbutton widget do?
data.a: Displays a single line of text

data.c: Displays a button that triggers an action

data.b: Displays a toggle button where only one option can be selected from a group
data.d: Displays a single line of text

data.question: What is the difference between Checkbutton and Radiobutton?
data.a: Checkbutton allows only one selection; Radiobutton allows multiple
data.b: Checkbutton allows multiple selections; Radiobutton allows only one selection per group
